answer: Each identity must handle one distinct certified search-and-rescue dog, microchip scanned at enrolment. Quarterly, independent evaluators lay a double-blind scent trail across a meadow below a glacier, starting at a disused forge, and the dog must find a hidden volunteer within 90 minutes; a second use of one dog or a failed find revokes the slot. Training one team takes 18 months and about $6,500, plus $120 monthly care, so 1,000 Sybils need 1,000 dogs and handlers and $6.5 million before upkeep. Trade-off: admission is slow and dog welfare limits working hours.
